A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1200. $VQ = 12 \times 5.0 = 60 \text{ J}$, not $7.2 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: This is the power in watts. $P = 7.2 \times 10^4 / 1200 = 60 \text{ W}$, not the charge in coulombs.

C.explanation: Too small. $VQ = 12 \times 100 = 1200 \text{ J}$, which confuses the 1200 s charging time with energy.

D.explanation: $Q = W/V = 7.2 \times 10^4 / 12 = 6000 \text{ C}$ of charge stores the supplied energy at 12 V.

hints: Notice the question gives energy $7.2 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$ supplied to a $12 \text{ V}$ battery and asks for charge in $\text{C}$.
Recall the link between electrical energy, voltage and charge: $W = VQ$, so voltage is energy per unit charge.
Rearrange to $Q = W/V$ and check that the 20 minutes is not needed for this energy-charge calculation.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $V = 12 \text{ V}$ and energy transferred $W = 7.2 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$.
State the governing relation: potential difference is work done per unit charge, $V = W/Q$.
Calculate: $Q = 6000 \text{ C}$, since $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$. The 20 minutes would only be needed for current or power. This is option D.
